question.text: Premium paid on commodity options is accounted for as:

answer.text: A financial asset on purchase; on exercise it is added to the cost of the call or reduced from the put sale proceeds, and is debited to P&L only if the option lapses or devolves without exercise
A capital expenditure to be depreciated over the option's life
An immediate expense in the period the premium is paid, regardless of exercise
Not recorded until the option is exercised

explanation.text: The Logic: A purchased commodity option is recognised as a financial asset on purchase. On exercise of a call, the premium is added to the cost of the underlying acquired; on exercise of a put, the premium is reduced from the sale proceeds. The premium is debited to the profit and loss account only when the option lapses or is allowed to devolve without exercise. The Trap: Option premium is not an immediate period expense, not a depreciable capital cost, and is not left unrecorded until exercise — it sits as a financial asset on the balance sheet between purchase and outcome. Note: The accounting outcome (cost adjustment vs. P&L hit) is driven by what happens at expiry, not by when the premium was paid.
